prerequisites: 0708314: Principles of Electrical Machines and Circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the principles governing the operation of electronic circuits in solving real circuits
Apply the basic principles of automation and control in solving real industrial problems
Recognize and understand the fundamentals and components of electronics applied in the general operation of electronic circuits
Recognize and understand the fundamentals of automatisms and robots applied in the management of robotized industrial machinery
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully solve new situations related to industrial engineering
Ability to manage NTIC-based environments and their emerging technologies
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the industrial technical engineering field
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in various situations or before various audiences
Apply the knowledge of industrial engineering in learning new methods and theories
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem critically and constructively
Apply the principles and methods of quality

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: INTRODUCTION. BASIC CONCEPTS OF INDUSTRIAL AUTOMATION.
Architecture of an industrial control system.
Block II: INTRODUCTION. MODELS OF PHYSICAL SYSTEMS. SYSTEMS ANALYSIS.
Review of signal and system concepts.
Negative feedback system. Unitary and non-unitary.
Block III: DESIGN AND TUNING OF CONTROL SYSTEMS. STUDY OF P, PI, PID CONTROLLERS.
Design of controllers using the Root Locus.
PID controller. Different forms of expression.
Physical meaning of proportional, integral, derivative actions.
Block IV: FUNDAMENTALS OF ANALOG ELECTRONICS AND ITS APPLICATION IN MECHANICAL ENGINEERING.
Review of basic circuit theory concepts, differential equations applied to electrical circuits, power factor concept.
Topic 2: SEMICONDUCTOR ELEMENTS. SMALL SIGNAL AND POWER.
Concepts of Diode, thyristor, small signal and power bipolar transistor.
Topic 3: BASIC CIRCUITS WITH SEMICONDUCTOR ELEMENTS.
Single-phase and three-phase controlled and uncontrolled rectifiers.
Parts of the analog signal measurement chain.
Sensors of position, displacement, temperature, pressure, flow, and level.
Difference between digital and analog system.
DC motor as an electric drive.
AC motor as an electric drive.
Information representation: binary system, hexadecimal system.
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 10% from objective multiple-choice tests, 70% from mixed tests (compulsory on-site control, problem-solving and multiple-choice questions), 10% from assignments (problem-based learning reports), and 10% from practical cases (short written exam on frequency converter configuration and data extraction). Objective tests are short, periodic exams with 5 questions and 4 possible answers. Assignments are graded on clarity, structure, format, technical accuracy, and completeness. Practical cases involve configuring a frequency converter and extracting values.
